metadata.title: Why does dropout work?
metadata.description: The trick is that there are three valid explanations and they all matter. Which ones you reach for tells the interviewer your level.

metadata.title: Design ML monitoring
metadata.description: Most ML systems fail silently. Monitoring is what tells you. The senior answer monitors data, model, and outcome layers separately.

metadata.title: How would you evaluate a search ranker?
metadata.description: Search ranking eval is offline metrics for development, A/B for shipping, and human raters for absolute calibration. The senior answer uses all three and respects what each measures.

metadata.title: Build an LLM coding assistant from scratch
metadata.description: The architecture decision space is large: model choice, context retrieval, IDE integration, evals. The senior answer scopes the use case before any of it.

metadata.title: How do you handle hallucinations in production?
metadata.description: There is no single solution. The senior answer is a layered system that catches different hallucination types at different stages.

metadata.title: Tell me about your most ambitious project
metadata.description: The interview is checking the size of problem you can hold in your head and the structure of how you describe it. Specificity wins.

metadata.title: How would you debug a model that's not learning?
metadata.description: The 'tell me how you'd debug' question is a behavioral round in disguise. The interviewer is probing your debugging instinct, not testing facts.

metadata.title: When would you fine-tune vs prompt vs RAG?
metadata.description: The most-asked LLM design question of 2026. The answer is a decision tree, not a preference.

metadata.title: When would you not use cross-validation?
metadata.description: Cross-validation is a tool, not a default. The senior answer names the cases where it's wrong, expensive, or misleading.

metadata.title: Design a content moderation system
metadata.description: Moderation is a multi-policy classification problem at scale, with appeals, human review, and adversarial users. The senior answer separates policy from model and treats human review as part of the system.

metadata.title: How would you build evals for a coding assistant?
metadata.description: Code is one of the few LLM domains where ground truth is verifiable. Use that. The senior answer combines verifiable metrics with human review for what verification can't catch.

metadata.title: Two-tower vs cross-encoder: when to use which?
metadata.description: The recsys / search architecture decision that comes up in every retrieval interview. The right answer is 'both, in sequence.'

metadata.title: Fine-tuning vs prompting: the deep version
metadata.description: Past the basic decision tree. The senior answer covers SFT, LoRA, DPO, continued pretraining, and the operational trade-offs each introduces.

metadata.title: Tell me about a time you disagreed with someone senior
metadata.description: The standard behavioral question. The interviewer is checking whether you can hold technical positions, push back productively, and update on new information.

metadata.title: Walk me through the bias-variance tradeoff
metadata.description: The classic warm-up question. The L4 answer is the formula; the L6 answer is what it tells you about model selection in production.

metadata.title: PagedAttention and the vLLM serving model
metadata.description: Treat the KV cache like virtual memory: allocate in fixed-size pages, share pages across sequences, eliminate fragmentation. The reason vLLM is the default LLM server.

metadata.title: Gradient clipping
metadata.description: Cap the norm of the gradient before each optimizer step. The simplest and most reliable defense against training instability.

metadata.title: Implement KNN efficiently
metadata.description: The naive solution is one line. The interview is about scaling: when does naive fail, and what do you do?

metadata.title: Expected Calibration Error (ECE)
metadata.description: How well do predicted probabilities match empirical frequencies? Bin predictions by confidence, compare bin-mean confidence to bin-accuracy.

metadata.title: Eigenvalues and the spectral theorem
metadata.description: Eigenvectors are directions a matrix only stretches. The spectral theorem says symmetric matrices have a full orthogonal eigenbasis with real eigenvalues.

metadata.title: Quantization: INT8, INT4, FP8, and the inference cost picture
metadata.description: Reduce model precision to shrink memory and speed up inference. The trade-offs are real but increasingly small with modern techniques.

metadata.title: Two-tower retrieval
metadata.description: Encode queries and items with separate networks into a shared embedding space; retrieve by approximate nearest neighbors. The default architecture for industrial recommenders and search.

metadata.title: WSD and WSD-S learning rate schedules
metadata.description: Warmup-Stable-Decay keeps the learning rate flat before a final decay. WSD-S adds single-path decay-and-return checkpoints when the final token budget is uncertain.

metadata.title: RAG: retrieval-augmented generation
metadata.description: The standard pattern for grounding LLMs in your own data. Reference page; the full essay is linked at the bottom.

metadata.title: Cross-entropy and softmax
metadata.description: The pairing isn't arbitrary. Cross-entropy is the negative log-likelihood under a categorical distribution, and the softmax+CE gradient simplifies to (p − y), which is why it's stable.

metadata.title: Encoder-decoder architectures
metadata.description: An encoder summarizes the input into a representation; a decoder generates the output conditioned on it. The structure behind translation, T5, summarization, and many multimodal models.

metadata.title: SVD and PCA
metadata.description: The singular value decomposition factorizes any matrix into rotation × stretching × rotation. PCA is SVD applied to mean-centered data.

metadata.title: Adam, AdamW, and modern optimizer choices
metadata.description: How Adam works, why AdamW is usually preferred, and which newer optimizers address memory, batch size, or curvature.

metadata.title: CNN architecture
metadata.description: Convolutions encode translation equivariance and locality. The structural inductive bias that powered the deep learning revolution in vision.

metadata.title: Matrices as linear maps
metadata.description: A matrix is a linear function from one vector space to another. Every operation in ML. Projection, rotation, basis change, gradient flow. Is matrix multiplication.

metadata.title: Linear regression
metadata.description: Predict a continuous target as a linear combination of features by minimizing squared error. Closed-form solution, MLE under Gaussian noise, and the foundation everything else builds on.

metadata.title: Precision, recall, and F1
metadata.description: The three metrics every classifier interview asks about. Their definitions, when to optimize which, and the F-beta generalization.

metadata.title: Mixed precision training: FP16, BF16, and FP8
metadata.description: How modern transformers train at 2-4× the throughput of FP32 without quality loss. The bit layouts matter; the loss-scaling recipe matters more.

metadata.title: All-reduce and other collectives
metadata.description: The communication primitives behind every distributed training job. All-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, broadcast. What they do, costs, and when each is used.

metadata.title: Maximum likelihood estimation
metadata.description: The dominant statistical principle: pick parameters that make the observed data most probable. Reduces to minimizing cross-entropy for classification and MSE for Gaussian regression.

metadata.title: Design a RAG system for legal documents
metadata.description: Legal RAG amplifies every standard RAG concern: precise citations, no hallucinations, regulated domain, dense documents with structure. The senior answer addresses each.

metadata.title: Rotary position embeddings (RoPE)
metadata.description: The dominant position encoding for modern LLMs. Encodes relative position by rotating Q and K in 2D subspaces and supports several context-extension methods.

metadata.title: Dropout
metadata.description: Randomly zero out a fraction of activations during training. The simplest stochastic regularizer; still standard in vision and many NLP architectures.

metadata.title: Monte Carlo and importance sampling
metadata.description: Estimate expectations by averaging over random samples. The simplest way to compute integrals you can't compute analytically.

metadata.title: Perplexity and bits per token
metadata.description: The standard intrinsic metric for language models. What it measures, what units to use, and why it's a poor end-product evaluation.

metadata.title: How do you decide what to work on?
metadata.description: The senior signal here is that you have an explicit prioritization framework, not just a list of interests. The L6 answer connects user value, technical leverage, and team strategy.

metadata.title: The attention mechanism
metadata.description: Compute a weighted sum of values, weights derived from query-key similarity. The single operation that powers transformers, retrieval, and most of modern ML.

metadata.title: How do you deal with class imbalance in 2026?
metadata.description: Match the treatment to the imbalance ratio, error costs, label process, and decision metric. Class weighting and SMOTE are only two options.

metadata.title: Mixup and CutMix
metadata.description: Two data-augmentation schemes that train on convex combinations of pairs of inputs and their labels. Strong regularization for image classification; sometimes used in audio and tabular.

metadata.title: Design YouTube's recommender
metadata.description: The canonical recsys design question. The real test is whether you'll dive into model architecture or scope the problem first.

metadata.title: KL divergence
metadata.description: Asymmetric distance between probability distributions. Cross-entropy minus entropy. The mathematical glue holding most of probabilistic ML together.

metadata.title: Ranking metrics: NDCG, MAP, MRR
metadata.description: Beyond binary precision-recall: how to measure ranking quality when order matters and labels are graded.

metadata.title: k-means clustering
metadata.description: Partition n points into k clusters by minimizing within-cluster variance. Lloyd's algorithm: alternate assigning points to nearest center and recomputing centers.

metadata.title: Normalizing flows
metadata.description: Generative models built from invertible transformations. Compute exact likelihoods and sample efficiently. At the cost of architectural restrictions.

metadata.title: Explain the reparameterization trick
metadata.description: How VAEs propagate gradients through a sampling step. The senior answer explains the why (you can't differentiate through a sample) and the how (move the randomness outside the parameters).

metadata.title: Confusion matrix and classification metrics
metadata.description: The 2x2 (or KxK) table of predictions vs. truth that every classification metric is computed from. The Rosetta stone of binary classification.

metadata.title: ResNet
metadata.description: Residual connections enabled networks deeper than 30 layers to train. Still the dominant backbone for transfer learning in 2026.

metadata.title: Transformer architecture: a senior-level mental model
metadata.description: Strip away the diagram clutter. A transformer is a stack of (residual + LayerNorm + (attention or FFN)) blocks. Understanding why each piece is there is more important than memorizing the diagram.

metadata.title: Backpropagation
metadata.description: Reverse-mode automatic differentiation applied to a computation graph. The algorithm that computes gradients for every parameter in one backward pass.

metadata.title: Expectation-Maximization (EM)
metadata.description: Iterate between estimating latent variables given parameters (E-step) and updating parameters given latents (M-step). The standard tool for latent-variable MLE when the latents are unobserved.

metadata.title: How do you evaluate an agent?
metadata.description: Agent eval is harder than chat eval because there are intermediate steps, tool calls, and long-horizon outcomes. The senior answer evaluates trajectories, not just final outputs.

metadata.title: Microannealing and midtraining
metadata.description: A short cooldown applied to a mostly-trained checkpoint with a small fraction of candidate data mixed in. The standard mid-training probe for whether a new dataset is worth including.

metadata.title: FSDP and ZeRO: sharding optimizer state, gradients, and parameters
metadata.description: How modern training scales beyond a single GPU's memory by partitioning the optimizer state, gradients, and parameters across the data-parallel group.

metadata.title: Bayes' rule and the posterior
metadata.description: How to update beliefs given evidence: posterior ∝ likelihood × prior. The foundation of Bayesian inference, naive Bayes, and probabilistic graphical models.

metadata.title: Long-context LLMs: training and serving techniques
metadata.description: What makes a 1M-token context model work. Position-encoding extension, attention kernels, KV-cache management, and the tradeoffs.

metadata.title: SVM and the kernel trick
metadata.description: Maximum-margin classifier with a kernel that lets it operate in implicit high-dimensional feature spaces. Beautiful theory; less common in 2026 production.

metadata.title: Policy gradient methods
metadata.description: Directly optimize the policy by following the gradient of expected return. REINFORCE, actor-critic, and the foundation of modern RL.

metadata.title: Diffusion models
metadata.description: Learn to invert a fixed noising process. The dominant generative paradigm for images, audio, video, and molecules in 2026.

metadata.title: Variational autoencoders (VAE)
metadata.description: Encode inputs to a latent distribution, decode samples back, optimize evidence lower bound. The cleanest gateway to deep generative models.

metadata.title: Implement attention from scratch
metadata.description: The coding question that doubles as a depth check. The code is short; the conversation around it tells the level.

metadata.title: Markov chains
metadata.description: Stochastic processes where the future depends only on the present, not the past. Foundation of HMMs, MCMC, and many sequence models.

metadata.title: Residual connections
metadata.description: Add the input of a block to its output. Lets gradients flow unimpeded through depth and made networks deeper than 30 layers practical for the first time.

metadata.title: Walk me through how you'd train a 100B parameter model
metadata.description: The question is about parallelism and memory, not about modeling. The L6 answer combines data, tensor, pipeline, and FSDP/ZeRO sharding into a coherent strategy.

metadata.title: How would you do cold-start for a new user?
metadata.description: Cold-start is solved by combining minimal explicit signal, demographic and contextual fallbacks, and aggressive exploration in the first few sessions.

metadata.title: Cross-validation strategies
metadata.description: Hold-out, k-fold, stratified, grouped, and time-series CV. And when each one is and isn't appropriate.

metadata.title: Debug this training loop
metadata.description: A live coding question with a paste of buggy training code. The senior signal is the order in which you find bugs and what your debugging procedure looks like.

metadata.title: Determinant and volume
metadata.description: The determinant of a matrix is the signed volume scaling factor of the linear map. Zero determinant means the map collapses dimensions.

metadata.title: Exponential family
metadata.description: A unified family of distributions (Gaussian, Bernoulli, Poisson, Beta, Gamma, etc.) with shared properties: sufficient statistics, conjugate priors, simple MLE.

metadata.title: L1 vs L2 regularization, beyond the formula
metadata.description: The math is identical to most candidates: penalty terms in the loss. The senior signal is the Bayesian interpretation, the optimization geometry, and when each is the right choice.

metadata.title: Linear attention (Linformer, Performer, kernel methods)
metadata.description: Approximate the softmax attention matrix with a low-rank or kernel factorization so cost is linear in sequence length.

metadata.title: What's the most over-rated technique in ML right now?
metadata.description: A trap question that rewards taste. Strong opinions, defended with reasoning, are the senior signal. Weak opinions or 'I don't know' both lose.

metadata.title: Mixed precision: what's actually happening?
metadata.description: Beyond 'use BF16'. The senior answer explains what stays in FP32, why loss scaling exists for FP16, and the memory split.

metadata.title: Vision transformers (ViT)
metadata.description: Apply a standard transformer to a sequence of image patches. Beats CNNs at scale; the dominant backbone for foundation vision models in 2026.

metadata.title: Design Spotify's homepage
metadata.description: A multi-shelf, multi-objective recommendation surface. The senior answer scopes the shelves first, then designs each as its own ranker with a meta-layer above.

metadata.title: Recsys in the LLM era: what changes?
metadata.description: Most of recsys hasn't changed; LLMs add new capabilities at specific stages. The senior answer names which stages benefit and which don't.

metadata.title: Prefill vs. decode: the two phases of LLM inference
metadata.description: LLM inference has two cost regimes with very different bottlenecks. Mixing them up leads to wrong cost models and bad serving decisions.

metadata.title: Central limit theorem
metadata.description: Sums of many independent random variables become Gaussian. Why nearly every error bar in ML and statistics is computed from a normal distribution.

metadata.title: A/B testing for ML systems
metadata.description: The framework for proving a model change actually helps. Statistical power, novelty effects, network effects, all the things people get wrong.

metadata.title: Derive logistic regression from MLE
metadata.description: Standard math-screen question. The senior signal is whether you can derive it cleanly and connect MLE to cross-entropy.

metadata.title: Grouped-query and multi-query attention (GQA, MQA)
metadata.description: Share K and V heads across query heads to shrink the KV cache 4-8x with negligible quality loss. Standard in modern decoder LLMs.

metadata.title: Tensor parallelism
metadata.description: Split a single matrix multiplication across multiple GPUs. The way to fit one transformer layer that doesn't fit on a single device.

metadata.title: Design fraud detection for a payment company
metadata.description: Fraud has the worst data of any ML problem: heavily imbalanced, biased labels, adversarial actors, and direct money on the line. The senior answer respects all four.

metadata.title: BatchNorm vs LayerNorm (and the transformer wrinkle)
metadata.description: BatchNorm and LayerNorm normalize different axes and behave differently during training. The axis and train/eval behavior determine which one fits.

metadata.title: RLHF, DPO, and the alignment training stack
metadata.description: How LLMs get from 'next-token predictor' to 'helpful assistant.' The post-training pipeline in 2026.

metadata.title: Universal approximation theorem
metadata.description: A neural network with one hidden layer and enough units can approximate any continuous function on a bounded domain. What it does and doesn't say about deep learning.

metadata.title: Generative adversarial networks (GANs)
metadata.description: Two networks compete: a generator produces samples, a discriminator distinguishes them from real data. Sharp samples, training instability, mostly displaced by diffusion in 2026.

metadata.title: Learning rate schedules: warmup and cosine decay
metadata.description: Why almost every modern training run linearly warms up the LR over a few hundred steps and then decays it on a cosine to near zero.

metadata.title: How would you evaluate an LLM application you've built?
metadata.description: A level-defining question. The same words elicit a junior, senior, or staff answer. The rubric below shows the differences.

metadata.title: Bias and variance of estimators
metadata.description: An estimator has bias (systematic error) and variance (sample-to-sample wobble). Mean-squared error decomposes into the two.

metadata.title: Activation functions
metadata.description: ReLU, GELU, swish, sigmoid, tanh. What each does, why GELU/swish replaced ReLU in transformers, and when to use which.

metadata.title: Tokenization: BPE, WordPiece, and the LLM era
metadata.description: The critical input layer between text and model. Tokenization mismatch is a frequent source of production LLM bugs.

metadata.title: Lessons from Marin 8B: what an open pretraining log actually teaches you
metadata.description: Marin trained the first open-source 8B model to beat Llama 3.1 8B and published every mistake. The transferable lessons aren't about TPUs. They're about how to run pretraining like a science.

metadata.title: Design a feature store from scratch
metadata.description: A feature store solves training-serving skew, feature reuse, and lineage. The senior answer explains why each property matters and what minimum viable looks like.

metadata.title: Positive (semi-)definite matrices
metadata.description: Matrices that define inner products and proper covariances. The geometry of PSD: ellipsoids, not arbitrary shapes.

metadata.title: Sequence packing with block-diagonal masks
metadata.description: Concatenate multiple short examples into one fixed-length sequence to eliminate padding waste. The single largest throughput win for training on skewed-length corpora.

metadata.title: Random forests
metadata.description: Bag deep decision trees plus random feature subsets per split. Variance averaging beats any single tree; the dominant out-of-the-box ensemble before GBDT.

metadata.title: Regularization: L1, L2, dropout, early stopping, and the modern view
metadata.description: The classical regularizers + the modern reality that SGD's noise is itself a regularizer. The hierarchy of choices when your model is overfitting.

metadata.title: Floating-point formats: FP32, FP16, BF16, FP8, TF32
metadata.description: How modern accelerators trade precision for speed. The bit layouts of every numeric format that appears in deep learning.

metadata.title: Bayesian vs frequentist: a practitioner's framing
metadata.description: The textbook distinction is philosophical. The practitioner distinction is whether you can sample from a posterior cheaply, and whether you need uncertainty for downstream decisions.

metadata.title: How would you reduce LLM inference cost by 10x?
metadata.description: The cost-engineering question. The L6 answer doesn't pick a technique, it diagnoses where the cost is, then picks five.

metadata.title: Sparse attention (BigBird, Longformer)
metadata.description: Replace the dense n×n attention mask with a sparse pattern that has O(n) non-zeros while preserving information flow across the full sequence.

metadata.title: Gradient accumulation
metadata.description: Run several forward-backward passes before each optimizer step to simulate a larger effective batch size without the memory cost.

metadata.title: Design Amazon's people also bought
metadata.description: A simple-sounding feature with deep recsys ground underneath. The senior answer chooses between item-item collaborative filtering, embedding similarity, and learned co-purchase models, with explicit handling of feedback loops.

metadata.title: Speculative decoding
metadata.description: Break the autoregressive serial bottleneck without changing the output distribution. 2-3× inference speedup, free.

metadata.title: Explain backprop through time
metadata.description: BPTT is just backprop on the unrolled computation graph of a recurrent network. The interview signal is whether you understand truncation and what it costs.

metadata.title: Matrix factorization for recsys
metadata.description: Decompose the user-item interaction matrix into user and item embeddings whose dot product approximates the rating. The original collaborative filtering.

metadata.title: Gradient boosting (xgboost, lightgbm, catboost)
metadata.description: Train trees sequentially, each one fitting the gradient of the loss with respect to the current ensemble's prediction. The dominant tabular learner in 2026.

metadata.title: Embedding spaces and similarity metrics
metadata.description: How learned vector representations encode meaning, and why cosine similarity is the default metric for retrieval and recsys.

metadata.title: Q-learning
metadata.description: Learn the action-value function Q(s, a) by Bellman backups. The foundation of value-based RL. DQN, Rainbow, and the original Atari breakthroughs.

metadata.title: Matrix calculus for ML
metadata.description: Gradients, Jacobians, and Hessians for vector- and matrix-valued functions. The minimum needed to derive backprop and second-order methods.

metadata.title: Label smoothing
metadata.description: Replace one-hot targets with a softened distribution that puts ε mass on the wrong classes. Improves calibration, sometimes hurts retrieval.

metadata.title: Weight decay vs. L2 regularization
metadata.description: L2 adds ½λ‖θ‖² to the loss; weight decay shrinks θ multiplicatively at each step. They are equivalent under SGD but not under Adam. Which is why AdamW exists.

metadata.title: Applied Scientist vs MLE vs Research Engineer: what these roles actually do
metadata.description: Companies use the same ML titles for different work. Compare the modeling, research, engineering, and product mix before choosing a target role.

metadata.title: Calibration: when your model says 80% it should be right 80% of the time
metadata.description: Accuracy isn't enough; you also want predictions to mean what they say. Calibration is the difference.

metadata.title: Probabilistic graphical models
metadata.description: Express joint distributions as graphs whose structure encodes conditional independence. Bayesian networks (directed) and Markov random fields (undirected).

metadata.title: Design a system for safe LLM deployment in healthcare
metadata.description: Healthcare adds three constraints on top of normal LLM deployment: regulatory compliance, low tolerance for harm, and a workflow that already has clinicians as the final decision-maker.

metadata.title: How do you choose a loss function?
metadata.description: Choose a loss from the target, noise model, error cost, and output constraints. A well-trained model still fails when its objective is wrong.

metadata.title: RoPE, ALiBi, and modern positional encodings
metadata.description: Modern LLMs usually replace sinusoidal positional encoding with RoPE, ALiBi, or related methods. Compare how they represent relative position and extrapolate.

metadata.title: The 5 things every applied scientist interview is actually testing for
metadata.description: Strip away the questions and the role-specific jargon. Every senior AS loop is checking the same five things. If you know what they are, the prep gets sharper.

metadata.title: How do you choose a learning rate?
metadata.description: The right answer is a procedure, not a number. The wrong answers are 'use the default' and 'try a few values.'

metadata.title: Exploding and vanishing gradients
metadata.description: Why deep networks were untrainable before residuals, normalization, and ReLU. The math of gradient magnitudes through depth and the standard fixes.

metadata.title: DBSCAN
metadata.description: Density-based clustering: form clusters from regions of high point density, label sparse points as noise. Handles arbitrary cluster shapes; no k to specify.

metadata.title: ROC, PR curves, and AUC
metadata.description: What ROC-AUC and PR-AUC measure, when to use which, and why ROC-AUC is misleading on heavy class imbalance.

metadata.title: Mixture of Experts (MoE)
metadata.description: Replace one large feed-forward block with N smaller experts and a router that activates only k of them per token. Trades parameter count for compute.

metadata.title: Object detection: Faster R-CNN, YOLO, DETR
metadata.description: Localize and classify objects in an image. The three main architectural families: two-stage proposal-based, one-stage grid-based, and transformer-based.

metadata.title: Autoregressive vs. diffusion generation
metadata.description: Two paradigms for generative modeling: predict the next element step-by-step (autoregressive) or iteratively denoise from pure noise (diffusion). Different costs, different strengths.

metadata.title: KV cache: how LLM inference avoids quadratic decode cost
metadata.description: A core optimization in autoregressive decoding. Without it, generating 1000 tokens would require O(1000²) attention operations.

metadata.title: Naive Bayes
metadata.description: A trivially simple generative classifier that assumes features are conditionally independent given the class. Fast, parameter-light, surprisingly hard to beat on text.

metadata.title: Pipeline parallelism
metadata.description: Split the model across GPUs by layer; pipeline mini-batches through the stages. The way to scale across slow interconnects when TP isn't viable.

metadata.title: FlashAttention
metadata.description: I/O-aware exact attention replaces O(n²) HBM traffic with a tiled streaming softmax in SRAM. It is a core transformer kernel optimization.

metadata.title: Z-loss
metadata.description: Z-loss penalizes the squared softmax log-partition value. It limits logit growth and can improve stability during long training runs or cooldowns.

metadata.title: Explain backprop in your own words
metadata.description: Backprop is reverse-mode automatic differentiation. It reuses forward-pass values to compute all parameter gradients at roughly one additional forward-pass cost.

metadata.title: System design case study: personalized search ranking
metadata.description: Design personalized search from retrieval through ranking, counterfactual evaluation, serving, experiments, feedback control, migration, and staff-level operating decisions.

metadata.title: Hidden Markov models
metadata.description: A latent Markov chain emits observations through a per-state distribution. Forward-backward, Viterbi, Baum-Welch. The classical sequence model toolkit.

metadata.title: Logistic regression
metadata.description: Linear regression for binary classification: pass a linear combination through a sigmoid, train by maximum likelihood. Still the strongest non-trivial baseline for tabular classification.

metadata.title: Negative sampling strategies: what actually matters
metadata.description: Choice of negatives often matters more than choice of model. The senior answer ranks the strategies (in-batch, hard, BM25-mined, model-mined) and explains the trade-offs.

metadata.title: How to think about LLM inference cost
metadata.description: Most teams calculate inference cost by multiplying token price by token count. The actual cost structure has five layers and most of the optimization wins are in the bottom four.

metadata.title: SGD with momentum
metadata.description: Add a moving average of past gradients to the update. Smoother trajectories, faster convergence in narrow valleys, and the foundation of Adam's first moment.

metadata.title: Decision trees
metadata.description: Recursively split the feature space along axis-aligned thresholds chosen to maximize a purity criterion. The base learner of GBDT and random forests.

metadata.title: Gaussian mixture models
metadata.description: Model data as a weighted sum of K Gaussians. Soft clustering, density estimation, and the canonical EM example.

metadata.title: Continuous batching for LLM serving
metadata.description: Let new requests join an in-flight batch at every decode step instead of waiting for the slowest one. The other half of why vLLM is fast.

metadata.title: Value-based vs. policy-based RL
metadata.description: Two paradigms in reinforcement learning. Value-based learns Q(s, a) and acts greedily; policy-based directly parametrizes the policy. When to use which.

metadata.title: Senior through senior-principal ML scope
metadata.description: Calibrate upper-IC ML interviews by problem ownership, technical depth, portfolio judgment, delegated authority, durability, and evidence rather than inconsistent company levels.
aliases: What L5 vs L6 means in ML

metadata.title: How do you scope an ambiguous problem?
metadata.description: Scoping is a core senior skill. The interview tests how you reduce ambiguity before choosing a model or system design.

metadata.title: Why is softmax + cross-entropy the right pairing?
metadata.description: The gradient simplifies to (p - y), and that's not a coincidence. The senior answer derives this and connects to GLMs and numerical stability.

metadata.title: GPU memory hierarchy: HBM, SRAM, and roofline reasoning
metadata.description: Decide whether an accelerator operation is limited by compute or by data movement across HBM, caches, and on-chip memory.

metadata.title: Design real-time personalization
metadata.description: Real-time personalization fails most often at the data infrastructure, not the model. The senior answer designs the feature freshness and serving stack first.

metadata.title: Why does Adam sometimes generalize worse than SGD?
metadata.description: Adam usually trains faster but in some settings finds sharper minima with worse generalization. The senior answer names the regimes where this happens and the modern fixes.

metadata.title: How do you A/B test a chatbot?
metadata.description: Chatbot A/B testing has all the hard parts of regular A/B testing plus delayed feedback, conversational state, and metrics that are hard to define.

metadata.title: Activation checkpointing
metadata.description: Trade compute for memory: drop activations during the forward pass and recompute them during the backward pass. The cheapest way to fit a larger model on the same GPU.

metadata.title: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
metadata.description: Constrain policy updates with a clipped surrogate objective. The default actor-critic algorithm in 2026. For robotics, games, and RLHF.

metadata.title: Walk me through speculative decoding
metadata.description: The interview signal is whether you understand why decoding is memory-bound and why the verify pass is essentially free.

metadata.title: LLM Evals: The hardest part of shipping LLMs, and why most teams get it wrong
metadata.description: Your model is only as good as your eval. Your eval is a product. Treat it like one. The patterns that separate teams that ship from teams that thrash.

metadata.title: Weight initialization (Kaiming, Xavier)
metadata.description: Set the initial variance of each layer's weights so that activations and gradients neither explode nor vanish through depth. The single most impactful one-line decision in deep nets.

metadata.title: Actor-critic methods
metadata.description: Policy gradient with a learned value baseline. The actor picks actions; the critic estimates how good they were. The architecture under PPO, A3C, SAC, and most modern RL.

metadata.title: Advantage estimation and GAE
metadata.description: Policy gradients need a low-variance estimate of how much better an action was than average. GAE is the standard answer: an exponentially weighted blend of n-step returns.

metadata.title: Alternating least squares for collaborative filtering
metadata.description: Factorize the user-item matrix into two low-rank factors. Each is a linear regression given the other, so alternate. The classical recsys workhorse before deep learning.

metadata.title: Anchor boxes and non-maximum suppression
metadata.description: Object detectors predict thousands of overlapping boxes. Anchors give each prediction a prior shape; NMS prunes near-duplicates. The pre-DETR pipeline that defined the field for a decade.

metadata.title: Approximate nearest neighbors: HNSW, IVF, and product quantization
metadata.description: Exact k-NN over a billion vectors is infeasible. ANN trades a small recall hit for a 100x to 10,000x speedup. The reason vector search at scale exists.

metadata.title: BERT and masked language modeling
metadata.description: Train a transformer to fill in randomly masked tokens. The result is a bidirectional encoder that broke a dozen NLP benchmarks at once and defined the pretrain-then-finetune era.

metadata.title: Convolution as matrix multiplication (im2col)
metadata.description: A 2D convolution is a matmul in disguise. Unfold the input into columns, multiply by a flattened filter matrix. The reason CNNs run fast on the same hardware as transformers.

metadata.title: Decoding strategies: greedy, beam, top-k, top-p, temperature
metadata.description: Same model, different samplers, very different outputs. The choice of decoder is often more impactful than the last percent of training. Know the tradeoffs.

metadata.title: Designing a RAG system that actually works
metadata.description: RAG fails most often at retrieval, not generation. A practitioner's guide to the architecture, the failure modes, and what production teams actually do in 2026.

metadata.title: Epistemic vs aleatoric uncertainty
metadata.description: Epistemic uncertainty shrinks with more data; aleatoric uncertainty does not. Confusing them causes miscalibration and wasted data collection.

metadata.title: Exploration vs exploitation: epsilon-greedy, UCB, Thompson sampling
metadata.description: An RL or bandit agent has to keep trying new actions to learn while taking the best-known action to score. Three classical strategies, each with a different way of resolving the tension.

metadata.title: Factorization machines
metadata.description: Linear models can't capture feature interactions. Polynomial models have too many parameters. Factorization machines find a middle path: factorize the interaction matrix and learn an embedding per feature.

metadata.title: Forward-backward and Viterbi: dynamic programming on chains
metadata.description: Sum and max over exponentially many paths in linear time. Forward-backward computes posteriors over hidden states; Viterbi finds the most likely state sequence. The same idea, two semirings.

metadata.title: Gaussian processes
metadata.description: A distribution over functions defined by a mean and covariance kernel. Predicts a mean and kernel-conditional uncertainty. Beautiful theory, brutal scaling.

metadata.title: Graph neural networks: message passing as A·X·W
metadata.description: Neighbors carry signal. A graph neural network averages each node's neighborhood and projects with a learned matrix. The same matmul as a CNN, on irregular structure.

metadata.title: Kernel methods and the kernel trick
metadata.description: Compute inner products in a high-dimensional feature space without ever materializing the features. The mathematical move that lets a linear classifier draw nonlinear boundaries.

metadata.title: Knowledge distillation
metadata.description: Train a small student to match a large teacher's outputs. The student gets richer signal than from hard labels because the teacher's soft probabilities encode similarity structure.

metadata.title: LSTM and GRU: gating as Hadamard products
metadata.description: Recurrent networks fail because gradients vanish through repeated matmul. Gates fix this by using elementwise multiplication to control information flow. Then transformers replaced them anyway.

metadata.title: Multi-head attention: why one head is not enough
metadata.description: Run h independent attention computations in parallel, then concatenate. Each head specializes in a different relation. The mechanism most senior candidates can write but few can motivate.

metadata.title: Pruning: structured vs unstructured sparsity
metadata.description: Set unimportant weights to zero, recover most of the accuracy. Unstructured pruning shrinks model size; structured pruning shrinks inference time. They solve different problems.

metadata.title: Self-attention vs cross-attention
metadata.description: Self-attention reads from one sequence; cross-attention reads from another. This input choice determines encoder-only, decoder-only, and encoder-decoder structures.

metadata.title: t-SNE and UMAP: nonlinear dimensionality reduction
metadata.description: Both project high-dimensional data to 2D for visualization by preserving local neighborhoods. Both are easy to misread. Know what they show and what they hide.

metadata.title: Word embeddings: Word2Vec, GloVe, and the geometry of meaning
metadata.description: Map words to dense vectors so that similar words land near each other. The breakthrough that proved meaning lives in geometry, not symbols.

metadata.title: Automatic speech recognition (ASR)
metadata.description: The end-to-end map from a waveform to text: features, the three modeling paradigms (CTC, RNN-T, attention), language-model fusion, and how the field moved from HMM-GMM pipelines to a single neural model.

metadata.title: Belief propagation (message passing)
metadata.description: Belief propagation computes graphical-model marginals through local messages. Sum-product is exact on trees and approximate on graphs with cycles.

metadata.title: Conditional random fields (CRFs)
metadata.description: A CRF models labels for a whole sequence and scores transitions jointly. Linear-chain CRFs improve taggers when neighboring labels constrain each other.

metadata.title: Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC)
metadata.description: How you train a sequence model to map audio (or pixels) to text without knowing the alignment. CTC marginalizes over every possible alignment with a blank symbol and a forward-backward sum.

metadata.title: Content-based filtering
metadata.description: Content-based filtering scores item features against a user profile. It handles item cold-start and often complements collaborative filtering.

metadata.title: Discrete gradient estimators
metadata.description: How to get gradients through a sampling step over discrete variables, where the reparameterization trick doesn't apply. Covers the score-function (REINFORCE) estimator, the straight-through estimator, and Gumbel-Softmax.

metadata.title: Factor analysis and probabilistic PCA
metadata.description: Factor analysis uses latent factors with per-feature noise. Probabilistic PCA uses isotropic noise and recovers classical PCA in its zero-noise limit.

metadata.title: Knowledge-graph embeddings
metadata.description: Knowledge-graph embeddings turn link prediction into vector scoring. Compare TransE, DistMult, ComplEx, and RotatE by the relation patterns they can represent.

metadata.title: Model interpretability

metadata.title: RNN-Transducer (RNN-T)
metadata.description: The streaming-ASR workhorse. RNN-T fixes CTC's biggest weakness (its frame-independence assumption) by adding a prediction network that conditions on previously emitted tokens, while staying naturally streamable.
